segments.text: Good Evening, This is Akash Vani, I am Shagun Chopra with the news at 9.
The Headlines
Prime Minister Narendra Modi praises brave pilot Smith Machur for saving hundreds of
lives and foiling attempt to crash Israel bound flight. Asserts Indians are those who
risk their lives to save others, not take lives.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says India is building manufacturing value trains from
designed to finish goods as a trusted link in global supply chains.
Nation pays homage to father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi and former Prime Minister Lal
Bahadur Shastri on their birth anniversary.
And in Asian games, India win first women's hockey gold in 44 years, wrestler Sujit Kalkal
and boxers Parveen Hooda, Lovelin Burguhain and Ankush Pankal also clinch gold medals.
India climbed to 5th position in overall medal standings with tally rising to 76 including 16 gold.
And now the news in detail. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today spoke with Captain
Smith-Mutcher over the phone praising his bravery and presence of mind in foiling an alleged attempt
to crash an Israel bound flight Dubai flight. The prime minister said Indians are not those who take
lives but those who are willing to risk their own lives to save others. He lauded Captain
You are fighting for your life and your life.
At that time, you did not care about your life,
you did not care about the life of all the others.
And the biggest thing is that you are proud of the 104 crore people.
And that is why I am proud of it.
I would like to hear from you.
I have a report that you are my first actor.
On Wednesday, Captain Machher got seriously injured after being stabbed by his co-pilot
in the cockpit of Flight Dubai Flight, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
The flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children.
The pilot is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called for a WTO compliant approach to
correcting global trade distortions at the concluding day of G20 Trade Minister's meeting
in Milwaukee, U.S.
Speaking on structural excess capacity and production, Mr. Goyal said that India is
the fastest growing large economy in the world, with a domestic demand-driven economy
serving 1.4 billion people.
He highlighted that India is building manufacturing value chains from design to finish goods
as a trusted link in global supply chains. He said India's manufacturing capacity
serves its domestic and global needs and India does not have structural access
capacity in the sectors identified by the G20 presidency. A report.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal highlighted that India's trade with G20 members
depends on a transparent, non-discriminatory and rules-based trading system.
He said most favoured nation treatment is a key guarantee of this system
ensuring that the same terms apply to the smallest trader and the largest trader.
Speaking on ending forced labour in global supply chains, Mr Goyal said India's commitment
to the elimination of forced labour is absolute and unconditional.
The minister reaffirmed India's commitment to a rules-based, fair, equitable, non-discriminatory,
transparent, open, inclusive and multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core.
He emphasized the importance of preserving policy space for developing countries to
grow and feed their people while upholding decision-making by consensus.
On the sidelines, Mr. Goyal held bilateral meetings with his counterparts from Australia,
Saudi Arabia and South Korea, among others.
Supranasekya, Akashwani News, Delhi.
This is Akashwani, giving you the news.
The nation pays homage to the father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary
today. A Sarvadhan Prarthana sabha was held at Bapu Samadhi at Rajghat in the national
capital. President Ropati Murma attended the Sarvadhan Prarthana this morning and paid
floral tributes to the father of the nation. Vice-president C. P. Radhakrishnan, Prime
Minister Narendra Modi, Lok Sabha speaker Oom Birla and other leaders also paid tributes
to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. The Vice-President and the Prime Minister paid tributes to Mahatma
Gandhi at Gandhi Ismriti in New Delhi this evening. Several other dignitaries also paid
tributes to Babu. Immemence singers as well as school students sung devotional songs during
the program.
The nation also paid homage to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri on his 122nd
birth anniversary today, he was born on 2nd October 1904 in Pandit Deen, the Alupadhyaynagar,
previously known as Mughalsaray in Uttar Pradesh. As a teenager, he joined India's freedom struggle
and participated in the non-cooperation movement in 1921. Following independence, he held several
important positions in Uttar Pradesh and later in the Union government. Prime Minister
Narendra Modi paid floral tribute to the former Prime Minister at his memorial Vijayghat
in the national capital this morning.
Cardi and Village Industries Commission Chairman Manoj Goyal today informed that a special
discount campaign has been launched across the country, including Cardi Bhavan at Kannott
Place in New Delhi.
The discount is available from today till 16th of next month.
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises said that during this period up to 20% discount
will be available on Cardi products and 10% discount on Village Industry products.
Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, DMRC has informed that entry and exit gates of all metro stations
of the Delhi Metro network are now open. It added that the interchange facility at New
Delhi Metro station is also available. Earlier today, Delhi Metro had informed that 12 metro
stations will remain closed until further notice.
This is Aakashwani, you are listening to news at 9.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Sedeesh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided
by this vision for Seva and Sushasana, the government has been ceaselessly working towards
achieving the goal of a Vixit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment,
this dedication is transforming lives. Today in our special series, we bring you an instance
of how this vision has been translated into action through the monkey bath.
Monkey bath on Akashwani began as a monthly radio broadcast and has not missed a month since.
It is not a policy address, it picks out something a common man has done well, explains
scheme in ordinary words and asks for help with sanitation, water or
self-reliance. Radio reaches where nothing else does. The program has given a way of
talking to the country that is neither a press conference nor a campaign. Before
Mr Modi, no Indian Prime Minister had ever spoken to the country on his
schedule. Sharing his thoughts on the hundredth episode of Monkey Bath in
April 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had said that whether it is about
schemes or any subject with which Man ki Baat got associated, turned into a mass movement.
talking to media, eminent actor Amir Khan said, Manqi Baat program has a huge impact on
people.
Manqi Baat has had a huge impact on the people of India, and a huge impact on people, and
this is a very historic thing that the Prime Minister has done.
Today, crores of Indians tune into Prime Minister's address, listening to stories of governance
success from across the nation.
An aspirational India listens to the tales of transformed realities.
Manki Baat is a monthly radio dialogue which has fundamentally transformed the public communication.
Anpamesh, Akashwani News, Delhi.
In Punjab Border Security Force or BSF has neutralized two Pakistan insurers today
in Tarantarandes sector, quoting BSF sources, Akashwani correspondent reports that they
illegally crossed over to the Indian side of the border, despite giving warnings
by the deployed security personnel to stop the continued advancing forces forcing BSF to open fire.
Information and broadcasting ministry has mourned the untimely demise of three members of the
information and broadcasting fraternity who lost their lives in a tragic road accident in Mizoram
yesterday. The vehicle carrying the officials fell into a gorge while they were on official duty.
The deceased are Dr. Angam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau,
and Central Bureau of Communication in Nepal, Nampibo, Marinmay, IIS Director News, Durdarshan
Kendra and all India Radio Eyes All, and Edge Lianvila, MTS, Central Bureau of Communication,
Field Office Eyes All.
The Gold Rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Naitrena, Goen, Japan as
As Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on day 13, clinching six gold medals in hockey,
boxing, wrestling and archery in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting
excellence.
Indian women's hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating China 1-0 in the closely
fought final.
Lalrensema Ihmar Zote scored the decisive loan goals for India, while goalkeeper Savita
Punea produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure
the gold medal. The victory marks India's first women hockey gold at the Asian Games
in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title. Earlier Indian wrestler Sujit Kalkal scripted
a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men's 65 kilogram freestyle event.
In boxing, Parveen Huda won the gold medal in the women's 65 kg category, defeating
Chinese Taipei's Nian Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush
West Bengal clinched the gold medal in the men's 80kg category, defeating South Korea's
Kim Min Se-yong by a split decision 4-0 in the final.
India star woman boxer Lovlina Burguhain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category,
defeating China's Bao Zi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final.
In archery, women's recurve team created history by clinching its made-in-Asian
games gold medal, the Tri of Ankita Bhagat, Kirti Mishra and Kumkum Hoot defeated world
champion South Korea 5-3 in the thrilling final. India also backed silver in the mixed
recurve team event, Kumkum Hoot and Dheeraj Bommadevra finished runners-up after going
down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final. Sipak Thakraw, India scored the bronze
medal in the men's quadrant event. In sailing, Netra Kumanan clinched bronze
in the women's dengue event. With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position
in the overall medal standings. The country's medal tally has risen to 76, including 16 gold,
25 silver and 35 bronze medals. President Draupadi Murmur and Prime Minister Narendra
Modi have congratulated the medal winners. The India Laterological Department IMD has
forecast heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh during the next two days. And now, before
